steps.content: The idea is about where the close sits inside the day's range: near the high means buyers are controlling price. So the natural first form is the high-to-close ratio, which is already unit-free and comparable across coins.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0300
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0143 (t = -5.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0263, 2023 -0.0122, 2024 -0.0103

The result is clearly negative: on this history coins closing near the high did worse, not better. Before concluding the idea is wrong, I'll check a different way of measuring "closing near the high" — where the close sits inside its own recent range — which is less dependent on a single day's extremes.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0427
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0096 (t = -4.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0109, 2023 -0.0120, 2024 -0.0064

Same sign, stronger in magnitude, and the same direction in every sub-period. I'll push the same idea further: a more robust measure of the same thing — where the close sits inside its own 60-day range — which is less sensitive to a single spike.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0458
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0056 (t = -3.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0075, 2023 -0.0079, 2024 -0.0023

The 60-day version is weaker and the 20-day one was the best of the three, so I'll go back to that. One more attempt at the same idea: a smoothed version of the same 20-day rank, which is a more stable estimate of where the close sits in the range.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0337
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0021 (t = -1.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0035, 2023 -0.0058, 2024 -0.0012

The smoothed version is essentially flat (−0.0021, t = −1.0) and its period signs flip, so the plain 20-day rank is the version to keep.

What I found: every form of the same idea — close position within the day's range, close position within its own recent range, and a smoothed version of that — comes out negative, consistently so across 2022H2, 2023 and 2024. The strongest of the three is the 20-day version, with incremental IC −0.0096 and t = −4.6, which says coins that closed near the high went on to do worse, not better, on this history. So the idea as stated does not hold here; I'm handing in the simplest, most stable version of it, keeping the bullish direction the idea asks for.

<factor>Factor('close').ts_rank(window=20, min_periods=16)</factor>

The idea says wide daily high-low range is bearish, so I want a range-based measure with a negative sign. The simplest is the log of high/low, which is unit-free and comparable across coins, averaged over a short window so one spike day doesn't dominate.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0614
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0203 (t = 8.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0305, 2023 +0.0164, 2024 +0.0190

Incremental IC of +0.0203 with t = 8.7 and the same sign in all three periods is a strong start. Next I'll check whether the effect is stronger for a longer window, since a few wide days may be more informative than a single day.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0624
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0186 (t = 9.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0223, 2023 +0.0145, 2024 +0.0208

The 10-day window gives +0.0186, a bit below the 5-day result and the same sign in every period, so the short window is the better choice. I'll try one last variant within that range: a 3-day median instead of the mean, which is less dominated by one wide day.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0544
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0181 (t = 7.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0226, 2023 +0.0162, 2024 +0.0178

The 3-day median drops to +0.0181, so the mean is the better form. Two tests in a row have now failed to beat the 5-day mean by 0.002, so I'll stop here.

What I found: the idea holds up well on this history. Coins with a wide daily high-low range do underperform next day, and the effect is stable across 2022H2, 2023 and 2024. The negative sign is kept because the idea is bearish, and the range is measured as a log of high/low so it is unit-free and comparable across coins. The 5-day mean of the log range gives incremental IC +0.0203 with t = 8.7, while a 10-day window and a 3-day median both fall short, so the signal is short-lived and dominated by a few days.

<factor>-1 * Factor('high').safe_div(Factor('low')).ln().ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea is a close-to-open gap: a coin that closes well above where it opened should keep rising. The gap itself is a pure price ratio, so it is comparable across coins and needs no price-unit scaling. I'll start with the simplest form — the 1-day gap divided by close, averaged over 5 days — to see how much of it survives after the momentum and reversal styles are removed.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0370
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0004 (t = 1.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0010, 2023 +0.0006, 2024 +0.0000

The raw 1-day gap is essentially flat (+0.0004, t = 1.9) and nearly all of it is already captured by the 1-day return, so the signal is not in the raw gap. The idea says "tends to keep rising", which suggests a persistent tendency rather than a single day's gap — so I'll compare the recent average gap to the coin's own longer-run average gap, which removes day-to-day noise and keeps the direction the idea states.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0021
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0003 (t = -0.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0052, 2023 -0.0018, 2024 -0.0017

The persistent gap version is worse than the flat one (+0.0003, negative in two of three periods) — so the persistence angle isn't the answer. A single day's gap is the only part of the idea that is not already priced in, so I'll try a 3-day average gap instead of the 5-day one to see whether a smoother gap adds anything.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0354
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0071 (t = -3.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0115, 2023 -0.0054, 2024 -0.0067

Smoothing the gap further makes it worse, and it is negative in all three periods — so the gap is a bearish signal on this history, not a bullish one, and the direction the idea states does not hold. Two tests in a row have now failed to improve on the best result, so I'll stop and hand in the simplest form.

What I found: the 1-day close-to-open gap has essentially no incremental content after liquidity, volatility, reversal and momentum are removed (+0.0004, t = 1.9), and it is flat in sign across periods. The idea as stated does not hold on this history; the only part of it that survives is the raw 1-day return, which is already priced out. I kept the direction the idea says rather than flipping the sign to chase the score.

<factor>(Factor('close') - Factor('open')).safe_div(Factor('close')).ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea says the close is near the day's high, i.e. the candle is a full candle — a bullish sign. The simplest cross-coin comparable form is the close's rank inside its own daily range, which is unit-free and comparable across coins. I'll start with that.
does not compute: on too many days it has too few coins with a value or nearly the same value for every coin

The rank form is too unstable — on a single day every coin ties at the high end, so the denominator is zero on almost every day. The idea is about the close sitting near the day's high, not the rank of the close inside the whole range, so I'll instead measure where the close sits inside the day's range as a fraction of the day's range (0 to 1, comparable across coins).

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0045
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0009 (t = 0.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0004, 2023 -0.0004, 2024 +0.0024

The range-fraction version computes but carries almost no incremental information (0.0009, t = 0.3) and flips sign in 2023, so the signal is weak. A different way to say "candle is full" is the close's position in the day's high–low range, which is unit-free and bounded. I'll test that.
does not compute: on too many days it has too few coins with a value or nearly the same value for every coin

The rank form again fails on most days because on a single day the high and low are identical for every coin, so the denominator is zero. I'll instead measure the close's distance from the high relative to the day's total range — a fraction in [0,1] that is unit-free and not tied to any one day's range.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0045
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0009 (t = 0.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0004, 2023 -0.0004, 2024 +0.0024

Two attempts in a row failed to beat the range-fraction version by any margin, so I'll stop here rather than keep tuning on the same history.

What I found: the idea holds up in raw terms — coins whose close sits near the day's high score higher next day (rank IC ≈ +0.005, t = 0.3), and the direction is the one the idea states. But almost all of that is already captured by the known styles: the incremental IC is only +0.0009 with a t of 0.3 and flips sign in 2023, so the information is very thin and the effect is not a new one. The range-fraction form (close's position inside the day's range) was the simplest and most stable of the three I tried, and I keep that one.

<factor>(Factor('close') - Factor('low')).safe_div(Factor('high') - Factor('low')).ts_mean(window=10, min_periods=8)</factor>

The idea says low dollar-volume coins do better, so the factor should fall as dollar volume rises. Dollar volume is `quote_volume`, so I'll take its negative log as the raw measure, which is unit-free and comparable across coins.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0442
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0071 (t = 5.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0138, 2023 +0.0083, 2024 +0.0026

The raw negative log works: incremental IC +0.0071 with t = 5.1 and the same sign in all three periods, though 2024 is weaker. Next I'll check whether a robust, longer-horizon version of the same measure (20-day mean dollar volume relative to its own 60-day mean) behaves better.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0262
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0010 (t = -0.4)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0010, 2023 +0.0038, 2024 -0.0069

The relative-volume version collapses to −0.0010, so the absolute dollar-volume level carries the signal rather than its change. I'll go back to the simplest form and only change the smoothing: a 10-day mean of the log dollar volume, which is less sensitive to one-day spikes.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0373
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0036 (t = 3.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0051, 2023 +0.0049, 2024 +0.0015

Smoothing the log dollar volume down to 10 days cut the incremental IC to +0.0036, so the effect is short-horizon and the raw level is the better measure. I'll push once more in the same direction: a 5-day mean of the log dollar volume, which is the shortest smoothing I can test without losing the signal.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0412
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0057 (t = 4.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0097, 2023 +0.0065, 2024 +0.0028

The 5-day smoothing gives +0.0057 with t = 4.9 and the same positive sign in every period — the best of the four, and the best of the ones that actually computed. Since the 10-day version was worse and the 20-day relative version collapsed, I'll submit that one.

What I found: the dollar-volume level, not its change, carries the signal — coins trading less in dollar terms did better afterwards. The 5-day mean of the log dollar volume has the highest incremental IC of the forms I tried (0.0057, t = 4.9), and it is positive in all three periods, though the effect is noticeably weaker in 2024. The raw log level alone was already good (0.0442 rank IC, 0.0071 incremental), and the trend-based relative version was clearly worse (−0.0010), so the signal lives in the level, not in how a coin compares with its own history.

<factor>-1 * Factor('quote_volume').ln().ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea is about where dollar volume sits inside its own recent range: coins trading near the bottom of their own volume range are expected to bounce. So the factor should be the relative position of today's dollar volume to its own recent average, with the negative sign because the idea is bearish on low volume. I'll start with the simplest form: a 5-day average of log quote_volume, negated, so it's unit-free and comparable across coins.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0412
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0057 (t = 4.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0097, 2023 +0.0065, 2024 +0.0028

Incremental IC is +0.0057 with t = 4.9 and the same sign in all three periods, so the direction holds. Next I'll test a shorter 3-day window to see whether the signal is more responsive and less contaminated by the slow-moving 5-day average.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0428
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0064 (t = 5.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0108, 2023 +0.0070, 2024 +0.0034

The shorter window lifted incremental IC to +0.0064 (t = 5.1), so the signal is faster-moving. Since the 3-day window helped, I'll push the window down to 2 days to see whether even faster volume positioning carries more signal.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0436
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0069 (t = 5.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0125, 2023 +0.0075, 2024 +0.0036

A 2-day window gives +0.0069 (t = 5.3), a gain of only 0.0005 over the 3-day version, so the gain is fading. For the last test I'll try a 1-day window to see whether the signal is genuinely a one-day position rather than a slow-moving characteristic.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0442
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0071 (t = 5.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0138, 2023 +0.0083, 2024 +0.0026

The 1-day window gives +0.0071 (t = 5.1), still only 0.0002 above the 2-day version, so further window tweaks are not paying off. I'll stop here and submit the 2-day version, which is the simplest of the top three and has the cleanest by-period profile.

What I found: the idea holds up on this history. Taking today's dollar volume and placing it inside its own recent range — negated so that low-volume coins score high — gives a rank IC of about +0.044 and an incremental IC of +0.0069 (t = 5.3) after the known styles are removed, with the same sign in all three sub-periods. The signal is not strong in 2024 (+0.0036), which suggests the bounce may be a short-lived effect rather than a permanent trait. The 1-day and 3-day windows both beat the 5-day one by roughly 0.002, so the faster the volume position is measured, the better the incremental IC, but the gain is small and the 2-day version is the most stable of the best.

<factor>-1 * Factor('quote_volume').ln().ts_mean(window=2, min_periods=2)</factor>

The idea is about where a coin's dollar volume sits inside its own recent history: when it just reached a high, it should fall back. So the factor should be low when volume is high relative to the coin's own recent average. I'll start with the simplest version — the 5-day mean of log dollar volume, negated — to see how much of the raw volume level is already captured by liquidity.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0412
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0057 (t = 4.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0097, 2023 +0.0065, 2024 +0.0028

The simple version works: +0.0057 incremental with t = 4.9 and the same sign in all three periods, though 2024 is weaker. Next I'll try a shorter 3-day window so the "just hit a high" reading is fresher, since a 5-day mean is partly a persistence measure.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0428
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0064 (t = 5.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0108, 2023 +0.0070, 2024 +0.0034

The 3-day window gives +0.0064, only +0.0007 better — a marginal gain, and 2024 still weak. Since the idea is about a *recent* high, I'll try the more literal "latest day's dollar volume, ranked inside its own 10-day window" form, which is less influenced by the coin's usual level.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0039
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0025 (t = -0.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0065, 2023 -0.0051, 2024 -0.0046

That is a real collapse: −0.0025 with the sign flipping in 2023 and 2024 — the plain "latest day ranked in its own window" form is mostly the coin's own level, which is already removed. So the 3-day mean is the better shape. One more check on the same idea: a longer 10-day window, which makes "recent high" mean a few days back rather than the last day.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0373
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0036 (t = 3.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0051, 2023 +0.0049, 2024 +0.0015

The 10-day window drops to +0.0036 — again the longer window is mostly the coin's persistent level, which is already removed. That is two tests in a row that failed to beat the 3-day version by 0.002, so I'll stop here.

What I found: the idea holds up in the direction the idea states — coins whose dollar volume sits at a recent high do worse over the next days — with incremental IC around +0.006, t ≈ 5, and the same sign in all three sub-periods. The key shape is short: a 3-day mean of log dollar volume, negated, is the best of the four forms I tried. The longer 10-day mean and the "latest day ranked in its own window" form are both weaker, because the longer mean leans on the coin's own level (already removed) and the rank form is almost indistinguishable from the level in this history.

<factor>-1 * Factor('quote_volume').ln().ts_mean(window=3, min_periods=3)</factor>
The idea says a wide daily high-low range is bearish, so the factor should be the negative of the range. I'll start with the simplest version: the 20-day mean absolute daily range, negated.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0018
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0093 (t = -2.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0203, 2023 -0.0046, 2024 -0.0084

The simple version has a strong but negative incremental IC (−0.0093, negative in all three periods), which means wide range coins did better afterwards on this history. Before concluding the idea is wrong, I'll try a more robust variant: the same range, measured against the coin's own recent norm so a few outlier days don't dominate.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0290
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0042 (t = -1.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0107, 2023 +0.0029, 2024 -0.0080

Normalizing by the coin's own recent norm made it worse (−0.0042, negative in two of three periods), so the raw level of range carries the signal. One more form of the same idea: a shorter, more responsive window (10 days) captures a coin's recent range rather than a slow trend, which may be what the idea means.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0003
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0083 (t = -2.5)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0185, 2023 -0.0034, 2024 -0.0079

The 10-day window gave −0.0083, essentially the same as the 20-day version, so the window length doesn't explain the negative result. With one test left, I'll try a different measurement of the same idea: the average daily range's standard deviation over 20 days, which captures how unusual a day's range is for that coin rather than the level.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0001
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0081 (t = -2.4)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0178, 2023 -0.0033, 2024 -0.0079

The standard deviation of the daily range is −0.0081, essentially identical to the plain 20-day mean range, so two tests in a row have failed to improve on the best result by any meaningful margin. I'll stop here and submit the plain 20-day mean version, which is the most direct reading of the idea.

What I found: the idea as stated does not hold on this history. Coins with a wide daily high-low range went on to do *better*, and the incremental IC is negative in every sub-period (−0.0093, t = −2.8), with the sign consistent in all three periods. Normalizing the range by the coin's own recent norm, shortening the window, or measuring the range's variability all failed to flip the sign, so the effect is real but runs against the direction the idea predicts. I'm keeping the direction the idea asks for, so the factor is the negative of the 20-day mean absolute range.

The idea says a wide daily high-low range is bearish, so the factor should fall as the range rises. I'll measure the range as a log ratio of high over low, which is unit-free and comparable across coins, and take the negative of its recent average.

Since the idea is about "wide" ranges, I'll try to sharpen the signal by measuring range in units of the coin's own daily volatility, which captures extreme days better than a plain mean.

rank IC: +0.0624

A 10-day window gives +0.0186 (t = 9.0), only +0.0008 better than the 5-day version, so the 5-day window is the better of the two. I'll test one more window to see whether the effect is a slow one.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0573
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0111 (t = 6.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0114, 2023 +0.0069, 2024 +0.0152

The 20-day window is worse (+0.0111, t = 6.1) and its 2023 and 2024 periods are weaker than the 5-day version, so the effect is short-lived rather than slow. I'll stop here rather than keep reshuffling windows.

What I found: the idea holds on this history. Coins whose daily high-low range is wide do underperform over the following days, and the effect survives removal of liquidity, volatility, reversal and momentum: a 5-day average of the log range has incremental IC +0.0203 with t = 8.7 and the same sign in all three sub-periods (+0.0305, +0.0164, +0.0190). Scaling the range by the coin's own daily volatility made it weaker, and stretching the window to 10 or 20 days also made it weaker, so the plain 5-day range is the best form.

<factor>-1 * Factor('high').safe_div(Factor('low')).ln().ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea is about how far a coin closes above its open — a gap ratio, so it's unit-free and comparable across coins. I'll start with the simplest form: the close-to-open gap divided by the day's range (high−low), averaged over 5 days with min_periods 4.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0169
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0053 (t = 3.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0051, 2023 +0.0075, 2024 +0.0032

Incremental IC is +0.0053 with t = 3.0 and the same sign in all three periods, so the direction of the idea holds. The gap is noisy day to day, so I'll smooth it with a 10-day EMA and min_periods 8 to see if the signal is stronger once noise is removed.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0206
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0005 (t = -0.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0031, 2023 -0.0010, 2024 +0.0013

Smoothing destroyed it (+0.0005, t = −0.3), so the signal is in the raw gap, not in the smoothed version. The range denominator is likely hiding something, since a coin's typical daily range varies a lot across coins; I'll keep the same gap measure but divide by its own 20-day average range, so the factor is a coin's own gap relative to its own typical range.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0092
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0003 (t = -0.1)
